text: This is Five Guys, the burger chain. One of the interesting things about Five Guys, very strange pricing. The burgers are hugely expensive because we perceive actually expensive burgers as being better. They are very, very good. When you ask for fries, you have three sizes to choose from, small, medium, or large. And they give you the appropriate size of cup, they fill it to the brim, and then they take another scoop and chuck it into the bottom of your brown paper bag. Why? The human brain disproportionately values the extra fries because they're the fries that you didn't have to give them. You have to fill the cup up because if you don't, you're shortch changing them. It's a genuine mark of generosity because it's a something you give someone that you're not legally obliged to do. And so what's fascinating about that is if you gave the job to a totally rational man, he'd make the cups larger. If you gave the job to your finance director, he'd tell you to stop giving away the free fries cuz they're costing us $3.7 million a year in potato costs. Both of those people would destroy net
